rationale: The assistant initially misread 'nn h98' as the model ('On your Panasonic NN-H98') rather than asking whether H98 was a display code, which is the sensible first step; the customer corrected this unprompted. Once the code and the cold-water test were reported, it correctly identified H98 as a high-voltage output fault and escalated to an engineer or Panasonic with consistent, appropriate safety warnings about not opening the case. It did not suggest a quick power reset, did not explain the magnetron-vs-inverter distinction or repair-vs-replace economics, but gave a safe and correct handoff with no parts pushed.
